guidance_summary:
GUIDANCE ANALYSIS: Deere & Company — Q1 2026

METRIC: Equipment Operations net sales growth
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: mid-single-digit net sales growth
UNIT: year-over-year percent growth
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Equipment Operations net sales; reported basis
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects 2026 to mark the bottom of the current cycle.
- Improving Small Agriculture & Turf and Construction & Forestry demand is expected to offset declining Production & Precision Agriculture sales.
- Positive foreign-currency translation supports sales.

METRIC: U.S. and Canada large agriculture equipment industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: down 15% to 20%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Challenging row-crop farm fundamentals and pressured producer margins are headwinds.
- Strong global crop production, robust commodity demand, normalization of trade flows, government programs supporting liquidity, improving used-equipment inventories, and an aging fleet provide partial support.

METRIC: U.S. and Canada Small Agriculture & Turf industry demand
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: flat to up 5%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry demand outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Dairy and livestock profitability is supported by strong beef prices.
- The turf market is experiencing a modest return to growth following several years of declines.

METRIC: Europe agriculture and turf industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: flat to up 5%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Steady interest rates, manageable long-term financing costs, and resilience in key arable markets are supportive.
- Recent declines in milk prices and newly negotiated EU trade agreements are not expected to have a material near-term effect.

METRIC: South America tractor and combine industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: down approximately 5%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook for tractors and combines
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The Brazilian market is expected to pressure demand.
- Subdued commodity prices, high interest rates, and a stronger Brazilian real are pressuring producer margins.

METRIC: Asia agriculture industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: flat to down 5%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The Indian market is expected to be only slightly below its strong 2025 level.

METRIC: U.S. and Canada construction-equipment industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: up around 5% year-over-year
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- U.S. infrastructure spending, declining interest rates, strong rental demand, and data-center construction starts support demand.
- Retail settlements are ahead of management's expectations and order books are growing.

METRIC: U.S. and Canada compact construction-equipment industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: up around 5% year-over-year
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- U.S. infrastructure spending, declining interest rates, strong rental demand, and data-center construction starts support demand.
- Retail settlements are ahead of management's expectations and order books are growing.

METRIC: Global forestry industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: flat
UNIT: year-over-year
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management maintained its global forestry-market outlook.

METRIC: Global roadbuilding industry sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: up around 5%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry sales outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Expected market increases in North America and Europe are the drivers.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture net sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: down between 5% and 10%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment net sales; reported-currency outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- North American large-agriculture demand remains subdued and South America is softening.
- The outlook was maintained because incremental North American improvement offset softer South American projections.
- The forecast incorporates positive price realization and currency translation.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture price realization
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: roughly 1.5 points of positive price realization
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture net-sales forecast component
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects positive North American pricing and positive full-year Brazilian price realization.
- South American discounts and targeted field-inventory reductions were implemented in Q1 but are not expected to continue through the year.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture currency translation
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: about 3 points of positive currency translation
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture net-sales forecast component
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- A weaker U.S. dollar versus relevant currencies, particularly the euro and Brazilian real, supports reported sales.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture operating margin
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: between 11% and 13%
UNIT: operating margin percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment operating-margin forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Tariffs, unfavorable regional/product mix, and higher warranty costs are headwinds.
- Improving North American production mix later in the year is expected to support margins.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture price realization
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 1.5 points of positive price realization, expected to be relatively even through the remaining quarters
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: the remaining quarters of fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture price-realization outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management said it does not expect pricing to be especially lumpy across Q2 through Q4.
- Positive North American pricing and easier comparisons from prior pool-fund accruals support the outlook.

METRIC: Production & Precision Agriculture operating margin
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: double-digit margins each quarter for the rest of the year
UNIT: operating margin percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: each quarter for the rest of fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: Production & Precision Agriculture segment operating-margin outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- North American production is expected to pick up and geographic mix is expected to normalize versus Q1.
- Management expects that improved mix to aid margins.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf net sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: up about 15%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf segment net sales; reported-currency outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Strengthened order activity in mid-size tractors, turf equipment, and compact utility tractors supports the outlook.
- Guidance was increased by 5 points versus the prior outlook.
- The forecast includes positive price realization and currency translation.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf price realization
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 2 points of positive price realization
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf net-sales forecast component
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Pricing is expected to contribute to segment sales growth.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf currency translation
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 2 points of positive currency translation
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf net-sales forecast component
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Favorable foreign-currency translation is expected to support reported sales.

METRIC: Small Agriculture & Turf operating margin
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: between 13.5% and 15%
UNIT: operating margin percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Small Agriculture & Turf segment operating-margin forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Higher shipment volumes, favorable sales mix, and price realization are expected to support margin.
- Higher tariffs are a partial offset.
- The margin guide was raised alongside the improved sales outlook.

METRIC: Construction & Forestry net sales
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: up around 15%
UNIT: year-over-year percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry segment net sales; reported-currency outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Strong construction and compact-construction retail activity and growing order books support demand.
- The segment was set up to produce in line with retail demand after underproduction in fiscal 2025.
- Guidance was increased by 5 points versus the prior outlook.

METRIC: Construction & Forestry price realization
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: about 2.5 points of positive price realization
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry net-sales forecast component
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Pricing actions are expected to contribute positively during the year.
- The full-year price forecast was revised down by 0.5 point because faster-than-expected backlog growth delayed realization of January price actions.

METRIC: Construction & Forestry currency translation
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: just over 2 points of positive currency translation
UNIT: percentage points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry net-sales forecast component
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Favorable foreign-currency translation is expected to support reported sales.

METRIC: Construction & Forestry operating margin
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: between 9% and 11%
UNIT: operating margin percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Construction & Forestry segment operating-margin forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Higher shipment volumes and production efficiencies support margin.
- Tariffs and competitive pricing pressure are headwinds.
- The margin outlook increased with the improved sales forecast.

METRIC: Worldwide Financial Services net income attributable to Deere & Company
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately $840 million
UNIT: USD millions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Financial Services net-income outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The outlook increased primarily because of a lower provision for credit losses.
- Favorable financing spreads are supportive, while lower average portfolio balances and prior-period special items are unfavorable comparisons.

METRIC: Tariff costs
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: around $1.2 billion
UNIT: USD billions, pre-tax
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Projected tariff costs
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Mitigation of Section 232 steel tariffs and some India relief are offset by volume growth.
- Management stated that the full-year projection was unchanged.

METRIC: Price-cost
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: price-cost neutral, inclusive of $600 million of incremental tariffs
UNIT: qualitative; USD millions of incremental tariffs
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Equipment Operations price-cost outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- A reduction in Construction & Forestry price realization moved the outlook closer to neutral.
- Slightly unfavorable production costs excluding tariffs, including some materials inflation, are partly offset by higher-volume overhead efficiencies.

METRIC: Net income attributable to Deere & Company
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: between $4.5 billion and $5.0 billion
UNIT: USD billions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP net income attributable to Deere & Company
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The outlook was increased following higher Small Agriculture & Turf and Construction & Forestry sales and margin outlooks.
- Large-agriculture conditions and tariffs remain headwinds.

METRIC: Effective tax rate
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: between 25% and 27%
UNIT: effective tax rate percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Company effective-tax-rate guidance
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management maintained the existing tax-rate guidance.

METRIC: Cash flow from Equipment Operations
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: between $4.5 billion and $5.5 billion
UNIT: USD billions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Equipment Operations cash-flow forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The range was increased by $500 million at both ends.
- Management expects inventory reductions to generate higher cash flow, offsetting lower net income adjusted for non-cash provisions.

METRIC: Research and development expenses
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: up slightly
UNIT: year-over-year
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Equipment Operations forecast
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Continued investment in technology solutions, product innovation, automation, and digital capabilities is expected to increase spending modestly.

METRIC: Capital expenditures
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately $1.4 billion
UNIT: USD millions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Company capital-expenditure estimate
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Capital spending supports property and equipment investment and continued product and technology development.

METRIC: Equipment Operations net sales growth
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: mid-single-digit growth for most quarters for the balance of the year
UNIT: year-over-year percent growth
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: most quarters for the balance of fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: Equipment Operations net-sales cadence outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Q1 benefited from easier comparisons following significant fiscal-2025 underproduction in Construction & Forestry.
- Management expects lower growth than Q1 as comparisons normalize.

events.title: U.S. temporary 10% import surcharge
events.summary: The White House proclaimed a temporary 10% ad valorem surcharge on most imported articles, effective February 24, 2026. The surcharge applies for 150 days and is in addition to applicable duties except where specified.

events.title: Deere declares $1.62 quarterly dividend
events.summary: Deere's board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.62 per share. The dividend is payable May 8, 2026, to shareholders of record as of March 31, 2026.
source_headlines: Deere & Company declares quarterly dividend of $1.62 per share

events.title: Administration announces farmer aid and calls for lower tractor prices
events.summary: Reuters reported that the administration was distributing $12 billion in aid to farmers and planned additional loan guarantees. The administration urged equipment manufacturers, including Deere, to lower prices. The report also cited higher fertilizer and diesel costs and continued trade uncertainty for growers.
source_headlines: Trump announces farmer support measures and calls on tractor makers to lower prices

events.title: USDA reports 2026 intended planting mix
events.summary: USDA reported intended 2026 U.S. corn plantings of 95.3 million acres, down 3% year over year, and soybean plantings of 84.7 million acres, up 4%. All-wheat planted area was forecast to decline 3%.
source_headlines: USDA: farmers intend to plant less corn and more soybeans in 2026

events.title: U.S. revises Section 232 treatment of steel, aluminum, and copper derivatives
events.summary: The White House revised tariff treatment for covered steel, aluminum, and copper articles and derivative products, effective April 6, 2026. The proclamation provided a 25% rate for certain derivative products, maintained other higher rates, and modified derivative-product scope. Covered derivative articles are subject to duties on their full customs value.
source_headlines: U.S. modifies Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum, and copper derivative products

events.title: Deere agrees to proposed $99 million right-to-repair settlement
events.summary: Associated Press reported that Deere agreed to place $99 million into a proposed settlement fund for customers who paid Deere or authorized dealers for certain large-agriculture-equipment repairs. Deere denied wrongdoing. The proposed settlement remained subject to court approval and included commitments concerning repair tools.
source_headlines: Deere agrees to proposed $99 million right-to-repair class-action settlement

events.title: USDA forecasts lower 2026 net farm income and higher net cash farm income
events.summary: USDA forecast 2026 nominal net farm income of $153.4 billion, down 0.7% from 2025. Nominal net cash farm income was forecast to increase 3.0% to $158.5 billion. Farm-sector working capital was forecast to decrease 9.2%, while debt was forecast to increase 5.2%.
source_headlines: USDA forecasts mixed 2026 farm-income outlook, with lower net farm income but higher cash income

events.title: USDA initial 2026/27 crop outlook projects higher corn and soybean prices
events.summary: USDA's initial 2026/27 outlook projected U.S. corn prices of $4.40 per bushel, compared with $4.15 in 2025/26, and soybean prices of $11.40 per bushel, compared with $10.40. The outlook projected lower U.S. corn production and exports, alongside higher soybean output, crush, and exports.
source_headlines: USDA's initial 2026/27 crop outlook projects higher corn and soybean farm prices

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Target period is Deere fiscal Q2 2026 (standalone 13-week quarter ending May 3, 2026), versus reported fiscal Q1 2026 standalone revenue of $9,611m. GUIDANCE bridge: FY segment outlook implies Q2 revenue of $13,000m: PPA $4,629m + SAT $3,443m + CF $3,389m + Financial Services $1,320m + other $219m. Thus change = $13,000m - $9,611m = +$3,389m. This uses Q2-weighted historical seasonality rather than pro-rating the fiscal year: Q2 2025 revenue was $12,763m and normally carries materially more equipment shipments than Q1. Subsequent events do not provide a defensible, incremental shipment or recognized-price amount before May 3; tariff events affect cost, while farm-income/crop-price information is too late or too indirect to alter booked Q2 revenue.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume, selling price, currency translation, and Financial Services revenue
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY segment sales outlook -> Q2 seasonal shipment/revenue bridge -> consolidated net sales and revenues.
assumptions: FY PPA sales midpoint = FY2025 $17,311m x (1 - 7.5%) = $16,013m.

Q1 PPA actual sales were $3,163m; remaining FY PPA sales are $12,850m. Q2 is assigned $4,629m using Q2 2025 seasonal sales of $5,230m, adjusted for the guide's lower PPA volume outlook and favorable currency.
Q2 Financial Services and other revenue are estimated at $1,320m and $219m, respectively, consistent with the FY Financial Services income outlook and lower average portfolio balance.
This is an ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE: FY guidance is first converted to annual segment amounts and then sequenced into Q2 using reported Q1 actuals and Q2-heavy historical seasonality.
event_contributions.calculation: Q2 forecast revenue = 4,629 + 3,443 + 3,389 + 1,320 + 219 = $13,000m. Change versus Q1 actual = 13,000 - 9,611 = +$3,389m. FY reconciliation: PPA FY sales implied at $16,013m; Q1 $3,163m + Q2 $4,629m leaves $8,221m for Q3-Q4.

event_contributions.affected_line: Production cost / COGS; not an identified shipment-volume driver
event_contributions.transmission_path: Temporary import surcharge -> imported-product and component cost -> COGS and operating profit; no defensible direct Q2 revenue recognition effect.
assumptions: The February 24 surcharge was announced after the February 19 guidance, but the supplied evidence does not disclose Deere's covered import value, pass-through, or dealer-order response.
Avoiding a speculative price/volume response, recognized revenue impact is set to zero.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ worldwide net sales and revenues = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Financing cash flow and retained earnings
event_contributions.transmission_path: Dividend declaration -> financing cash flow/equity distribution -> no revenue recognition and no GAAP income-statement effect.
assumptions: The dividend is a distribution to shareholders, not an operating expense.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ worldwide net sales and revenues = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential selling price and agricultural-equipment demand
event_contributions.transmission_path: Farmer aid / possible loan guarantees may support liquidity; administration request for lower prices could pressure realized price -> dealer orders and equipment revenue, if Deere changes commercial terms.
assumptions: Management's February guidance already incorporated government-program support for farmer liquidity and challenging row-crop fundamentals.
The report contains no Deere price concession, revised order book, or disclosed Q2 shipment change.
The announcement occurred late in Q2, so any demand response would principally affect orders and later shipments.
event_contributions.calculation: Incremental Q2 recognized revenue effect = $0m; narrative change is little, but not quantifiable before the May 3 quarter-end.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential Production & Precision Ag sales volume and dealer inventory
event_contributions.transmission_path: Corn/soy acreage mix -> grower cash-flow and machinery utilization expectations -> potential equipment orders -> future revenue.
assumptions: Combined intended corn plus soybean acres are broadly unchanged: 95.3m corn acres plus 84.7m soybean acres = 180.0m acres.
The guidance already assumed subdued North American large-ag demand; the planting mix alone does not quantify Deere unit demand or Q2 dealer shipments.
event_contributions.calculation: Incremental Q2 recognized revenue effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: COGS / imported derivative-product cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: Revised Section 232 treatment -> cost of covered imported articles and derivatives -> COGS; no disclosed direct revenue change.
assumptions: The modified treatment became effective April 6, leaving only part of Q2 affected.
No import-value, price-pass-through, or Q2 shipment disclosure is available; therefore revenue is not adjusted.
This is kept separate from E1: only Section 232 derivative-product scope/rate changes not already represented by the broad temporary surcharge are considered.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ worldwide net sales and revenues = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Selling, administrative and general expense / accrued liability
event_contributions.transmission_path: Proposed repair settlement fund -> legal expense/accrual -> operating profit and net income; no immediate equipment-sales revenue effect.
assumptions: The reported $99m fund is modeled as a discrete Q2 expense in the central case, subject to approval/accounting recognition.
No Q2 aftermarket revenue effect is assumed because repair-tool commitments do not establish a measurable near-term revenue amount.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ worldwide net sales and revenues = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential equipment demand and Financial Services credit quality
event_contributions.transmission_path: Farm income, cash income, working capital, and debt outlook -> farmer purchasing capacity / credit risk -> future equipment revenue and credit-loss provision.
assumptions: Guidance already incorporated challenging farm fundamentals, government-program liquidity support, possible lower sales volume, incentives, and elevated write-offs.
The mixed forecast does not identify Deere bookings or a measurable Q2 shipment response.
event_contributions.calculation: Incremental Q2 recognized revenue effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential PPA demand / farmer cash-flow expectations
event_contributions.transmission_path: Higher projected 2026/27 crop prices -> prospective grower income and sentiment -> equipment-order demand -> future revenue.
assumptions: The May 12 crop-year outlook arrived in the final weeks of fiscal Q2 and relates principally to the next crop marketing year.
It is supportive to the medium-term agricultural narrative but cannot defensibly be converted into a May 3 recognized-sales amount.
event_contributions.calculation: Incremental Q2 recognized revenue effect = $0m.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Target is standalone fiscal Q2 2026 GAAP diluted EPS, compared with fiscal Q1 2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $2.42. Guidance midpoint implies Q2 GAAP net income of $1,550m and diluted EPS of $5.72 using 271.0m diluted shares: $1,550m / 271.0m = $5.72; GUIDANCE change = $5.72 - $2.42 = +$3.30. Incremental Q2 news effect is -$0.30 per share: E1 -$0.02, E5 -$0.01, and E6 -$0.27. Total change = +$3.30 - $0.02 - $0.01 - $0.27 = +$3.00 per share, implying Q2 EPS of about $5.42.

event_contributions.affected_line: Net income, tax expense, and diluted share count
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY GAAP net-income guidance -> less reported Q1 GAAP net income -> seasonally allocate remaining FY profit to Q2 -> divide by diluted shares -> Q2 diluted EPS.
assumptions: FY net-income guidance midpoint = $4,750m.
Reported Q1 net income attributable to Deere was $656m, leaving $4,094m for Q2-Q4.
Q2 receives $1,550m of the remaining amount, reflecting Q2's historically stronger seasonal income contribution rather than equal quarterly pro-rating; $2,544m remains for Q3-Q4.
Diluted weighted-average shares are held at approximately 271.0m, close to Q1's 270.9m.
This is an ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE.
event_contributions.calculation: Q2 guided EPS = $1,550m / 271.0m shares = $5.72. Change versus Q1 EPS = $5.72 - $2.42 = +$3.30. FY reconciliation = Q1 $656m + Q2 $1,550m + Q3-Q4 $2,544m = $4,750m.

event_contributions.affected_line: COGS / production cost and income tax
event_contributions.transmission_path: Temporary import surcharge -> incremental Q2 COGS -> lower pretax income -> tax shield at 26% -> lower net income -> diluted EPS.
assumptions: Central estimate of Q2 pretax incremental surcharge cost is $6m, representing the portion economically incurred from February 24 through May 3.
This is incremental to February 19 guidance; it does not duplicate the tariff costs already embedded in management's guide.
Effective tax rate assumed at the guidance midpoint of 26%; diluted shares = 271.0m.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Q2 after-tax income effect = -$6m x (1 - 0.26) = -$4.44m. EPS effect = -$4.44m / 271.0m = -$0.016, rounded to -$0.02.

event_contributions.affected_line: Financing cash flow / equity distribution
event_contributions.transmission_path: Dividend payment -> retained earnings and financing cash flow -> no GAAP net-income or diluted-EPS recognition.
assumptions: Dividend payments do not reduce GAAP earnings per share when declared or paid.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ diluted EPS = $0.00.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential realized price, sales volume, and credit-loss provision
event_contributions.transmission_path: Aid and financing support could improve demand/credit; lower-price request could reduce price realization -> operating income and Financial Services provision -> net income -> EPS.
assumptions: No Deere price action, changed guidance, or quantified credit-cost change was disclosed.
Management guidance already contemplated farmer-liquidity support and weak row-crop economics.
Late-quarter timing prevents a defensible recognized Q2 impact.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ diluted EPS = $0.00.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential PPA volume and dealer inventory
event_contributions.transmission_path: Planting mix -> grower profitability expectations -> dealer orders / inventory -> future operating income -> EPS.
assumptions: Broadly flat combined corn-and-soy acreage does not provide a direct Deere unit-demand conversion.
Guidance already captured subdued large-ag demand.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ diluted EPS = $0.00.

event_contributions.affected_line: COGS / production cost and income tax
event_contributions.transmission_path: Section 232 derivative-product treatment -> incremental Q2 input or whole-good cost -> pretax income -> tax shield -> EPS.
assumptions: Central incremental Q2 pretax cost is $4m because the change took effect April 6 and Deere-specific covered customs values are undisclosed.
The estimate excludes E1's broad surcharge effect and excludes tariff expense already contemplated in guidance.
Tax rate = 26%; diluted shares = 271.0m.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Q2 after-tax effect = -$4m x (1 - 0.26) = -$2.96m. EPS effect = -$2.96m / 271.0m = -$0.011, rounded to -$0.01.

event_contributions.affected_line: Selling, administrative and general expense / legal accrual and income tax
event_contributions.transmission_path: Proposed $99m settlement fund -> Q2 legal expense and accrued liability -> lower pretax income -> tax shield -> lower net income -> lower diluted EPS.
assumptions: Central case recognizes the entire $99m as a Q2 discrete pretax charge after the agreement; actual recognition remains contingent on accounting and court-approval considerations.
The charge is not presumed embedded in February guidance because the proposed settlement was reported April 7.
Tax rate = 26%; diluted shares = 271.0m.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. After-tax income effect = -$99m x (1 - 0.26) = -$73.26m. EPS effect = -$73.26m / 271.0m = -$0.270, rounded to -$0.27.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential sales volume and provision for credit losses
event_contributions.transmission_path: Farm-income/cash-income outlook -> customer liquidity and credit quality -> potential equipment demand and Financial Services provision -> net income -> EPS.
assumptions: The report is mixed and does not provide a Deere-specific default, order, or financing-volume measure.
The guided Financial Services outlook already included favorable provision trends and unfavorable portfolio balances.
event_contributions.calculation: Δ diluted EPS = $0.00.

event_contributions.affected_line: Potential PPA volume and Financial Services credit loss

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Target is standalone fiscal Q2 2026 PPA segment operating profit, versus Q1 2026 reported PPA operating profit of $139m. GUIDANCE bridge produces Q2 PPA sales of $4,629m and a 14.0% operating margin, or $648m operating profit; management's FY margin midpoint is 12%, but stated double-digit margins in each remaining quarter and better North American production/geographic mix support a higher Q2 seasonal margin. News effects are E1 -$6m, E5 -$4m, and E6 -$99m. Total change = +$509m - $6m - $4m - $99m = +$400m, implying Q2 PPA operating profit of $539m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA sales volume, price, currency, production mix, tariffs, warranty, and production cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY PPA sales and operating-margin outlook -> annual operating-profit pool -> use Q1 actual and Q2 seasonality/mix normalization -> Q2 PPA operating profit.
assumptions: FY PPA sales midpoint = $17,311m x 92.5% = $16,013m.
Q2 PPA revenue = $4,629m, as derived in the consolidated-revenue bridge.

Q2 operating margin is set at 14.0%, above the 12.0% FY midpoint because management expected double-digit margins in every remaining quarter and cited improving North American production and normalizing geographic mix after Q1.

FY operating-profit consistency check: $16,013m x 12.0% = $1,922m; after Q1 $139m and Q2 $648m, the $1,135m residual for Q3-Q4 implies 13.8% on $8,221m of residual sales, consistent with management's expected later-year production-mix improvement.
This is an ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE.
event_contributions.calculation: Q2 guided PPA operating profit = $4,629m x 14.0% = $648m. Change versus Q1 = $648m - $139m = +$509m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA production cost / COGS
event_contributions.transmission_path: Temporary import surcharge -> incremental cost on covered imported PPA whole goods/components -> PPA cost of sales -> lower PPA operating profit.
assumptions: $6m Q2 pretax surcharge cost is allocated to PPA because the affected line is equipment production cost; no revenue pass-through is assumed.
This is incremental to guidance, not a reallocation of the $1.2bn tariff-cost outlook discussed by management.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Incremental Q2 PPA COGS = +$6m; Δ PPA operating profit = -$6m.
